note: FNS Section 1066 is a QC variance determination procedure describing how Quality Control reviewers should evaluate cases with multiple income types (earned, unearned, annualized/prorated). The Comparison I and Comparison II framework, error threshold testing, and examples are all QC audit methodology — they tell reviewers how to determine whether a variance exists and whether it constitutes an error. None of this is caseworker policy. The underlying policy concept (that households may have multiple income types that must all be counted) is already covered in the OLG: 'How SNAP Benefits are Calculated' explains adding earned and unearned income together, and BEACON data entry procedures exist for both earned and unearned income types. The QC review procedures themselves (separate evaluation per income type, comparison testing against error thresholds) have no caseworker equivalent and would not appear in the OLG.
